title: Steady-state VO2 above MLSS: evidence that critical speed better represents maximal metabolic steady state in well-trained runners
authors: Nixon RJ, Kranen SH, Vanhatalo A, Jones AM
population: Ten well-trained male distance runners completing 9-12 constant-speed treadmill tests
findings: Running speed at CS was 16.4 +/- 1.3 km/h versus 15.2 +/- 0.9 km/h at MLSS (P < 0.001).
At 0.5 km/h above MLSS blood lactate was higher and rose over time, but pulmonary VO2 did not change significantly between 10 and 30 min at either MLSS or MLSS + 0.5 km/h.
VO2 rose significantly and reached VO2max at end-exercise at about 0.4 km/h above CS, but remained stable at about 0.5 km/h below CS.
The authors conclude MLSS underestimates the maximal metabolic steady state and CS more closely represents it when defined by VO2 stability.
limitations: Ten well-trained men on a treadmill; recreational runners, women and trail or ultra settings not tested; runs were up to 30 min; MLSS-based criteria are contested.
implications: Place the upper limit of sustained (threshold) running at or just below CS rather than at an MLSS-style pace: in these runners CS was about 1.2 km/h (about 8%) faster than MLSS (computed from the two reported means).

Keep a safety margin when prescribing continuous work near CS (VO2 stable 0.5 km/h below CS; VO2max reached at 0.4 km/h above); a margin of about 0.5 km/h is supported only for well-trained men and only for up to 30 min.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (EJAP vol 121 pp 3133-3144, online 2021-08-05). Abstract confirms all numbers; 1.2 km/h and 8% are derived.
